blocks.text: A pathologist is handed three unlabelled slides of muscle. One has long cross-striated cylinders with nuclei at the edge, one has branching striated cells joined by dark transverse lines, and one has pale spindles with no striations. Naming each correctly depends on knowing how the contractile machinery is arranged and how the cells are connected and innervated.

blocks.markdown: All muscle cells contract by actin-myosin sliding, but they differ in organisation. **Skeletal muscle** fibres are long multinucleated syncytia with nuclei at the periphery, under voluntary control through **somatic motor neurons** at neuromuscular junctions; progenitor **satellite cells** lie beside them. **Cardiac muscle** cells (cardiomyocytes) are branched, usually have one or two central nuclei, and contract involuntarily; **smooth muscle** cells are spindle-shaped with one central nucleus and no striations. Cardiac and smooth muscle are supplied by the **autonomic** nervous system, which modulates rather than initiates contraction (cardiac pacemaker cells set the rhythm).

rows: Larger T tubules at Z discs, forming diads
blocks.caption: Comparison of the three muscle types

blocks.markdown: **The sarcomere** is the contractile unit between two **Z discs**. **Thin filaments** (actin) attach to the Z disc; **thick filaments** (myosin) lie in the centre. The **A band** is the dark band whose width equals the thick filament length (about 1.6 micrometres), including regions of overlap. The **I band** is the light band containing only thin filaments, bisected by the Z disc. The **H zone** is the pale central region of the A band where there are only thick filaments, and the **M line** at its centre anchors the thick filaments. When a muscle contracts, thin filaments slide over thick ones: the I band and H zone shorten, the Z discs approach, and the A band keeps a constant width.

blocks.latex: L_{\text{sarcomere}} = L_A + L_I \qquad (L_I = \text{two half I-bands, one on each side of the A band})
blocks.caption: Sarcomere length is the A band plus the total I-band width

blocks.title: Sarcomere shortening
blocks.prompt: A relaxed sarcomere is 2.2 micrometres long and the A band is 1.6 micrometres. What is the total I-band width, and what is it if the sarcomere contracts to 1.8 micrometres?

steps.text: Total I band = sarcomere length minus A band = 2.2 - 1.6 = 0.6 micrometres.
The A band does not change during contraction, so at 1.8 micrometres the I band is 1.8 - 1.6 = 0.2 micrometres.

blocks.markdown: **Excitation-contraction coupling.** In skeletal muscle, an invagination of the sarcolemma, the **T tubule**, carries the action potential into the fibre and lies between two **terminal cisternae** of the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR); this arrangement is a **triad**, located at the A-I junction. In cardiac muscle a T tubule pairs with one SR cisterna at the Z disc to form a **diad**.

blocks.title: Intercalated discs define cardiac muscle
blocks.text: An intercalated disc is a stepped junction between the ends of adjacent cardiomyocytes. It contains fascia adherens (anchoring actin of the terminal sarcomere) and desmosomes, which resist the mechanical stress of repeated contraction, and gap junctions, which allow ions to flow between cells so that the muscle works as an electrical syncytium. In sections the discs appear as dark transverse lines.

blocks.title: Identifying cardiac muscle
blocks.prompt: A section shows cross-striated cells that branch and have a single central nucleus, joined end to end by dark transverse lines. What is the tissue and what are the lines?

steps.text: Striations rule out smooth muscle; branching and central nuclei rule out skeletal muscle.
The dark transverse lines between cells are intercalated discs, so the tissue is cardiac muscle.

items: Skeletal: multinucleate, peripheral nuclei, voluntary, somatic motor innervation.
Cardiac: branched, central nuclei, intercalated discs, autonomic modulation.
Smooth: spindle, no striations, central nucleus, autonomic innervation.

blocks.title: Common exam trap
blocks.text: The A band does not shorten in contraction; the I band and H zone do. Do not confuse the A band with the thick filament zone only: the A band includes overlap with thin filaments, while the H zone is the part without thin filaments.

points: Skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle differ in cell shape, nuclei, striations, junctions and innervation.
The sarcomere runs Z disc to Z disc; the A band is constant, whereas the I band and H zone shorten as thin filaments slide over thick filaments; the M line anchors thick filaments.
Intercalated discs (fascia adherens, desmosomes, gap junctions) define cardiac muscle; skeletal muscle has triads at the A-I junction and cardiac muscle has diads at the Z disc.

questions.stem: A section shows short cross-striated cells with a single central nucleus, branching, and dark stepped lines where neighbouring cells meet. Which tissue is this?

distractorRationale.b: Skeletal fibres are long, unbranched with peripheral nuclei.

questions.explanation: Striations with branching, central nuclei and intercalated discs identify cardiac muscle. The stepped dark lines are intercalated discs.

questions.stem: Which muscle type receives voluntary control through somatic motor neurons at neuromuscular junctions and has multiple peripheral nuclei per fibre?
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle fibres are multinucleate syncytia innervated by somatic motor neurons. Cardiac and smooth muscle receive autonomic input.

questions.stem: Electron micrographs of a muscle during contraction compared with relaxation show which band keeping a constant width?

options.text: Distance between Z disc and M line

distractorRationale.a: Correct: thick filament length is constant.
distractorRationale.c: The H zone shortens as thin filaments move in.

questions.explanation: The A band equals the length of the thick filaments, which does not change. Shortening comes from thin filaments sliding inward, narrowing the I band and H zone.

questions.stem: Which description fits the H zone?

options.text: The pale central region of the A band containing only thick filaments
The region between two Z discs containing only thin filaments
The dark line anchoring thin filaments

questions.correctOptionText: The pale central region of the A band containing only thick filaments

distractorRationale.a: Correct; the M line lies at its centre.
distractorRationale.b: That describes an I band region.
distractorRationale.c: Thin filaments anchor at the Z disc.

questions.explanation: The H zone is the middle of the A band where thin filaments do not reach. It narrows or disappears during contraction.

questions.stem: A resting sarcomere measures 2.5 micrometres and its A band measures 1.6 micrometres. In a strongly contracted state the sarcomere measures 2.0 micrometres. By how many micrometres has the total I-band width fallen?
questions.explanation: The A band is constant, so all the shortening comes from the I band: it falls from 2.5 - 1.6 = 0.9 to 2.0 - 1.6 = 0.4 micrometres, a reduction of 0.5 micrometres. This is the sliding filament model quantified.

questions.stem: Which statement about intercalated discs is correct?

options.text: Fascia adherens and desmosomes provide mechanical coupling while gap junctions provide electrical coupling
They contain only gap junctions and no anchoring junctions
They are found between skeletal muscle fibres
They contain T tubules and terminal cisternae

questions.correctOptionText: Fascia adherens and desmosomes provide mechanical coupling while gap junctions provide electrical coupling

distractorRationale.b: Anchoring junctions are essential to resist contraction forces.
distractorRationale.c: They are specific to cardiac muscle.

questions.explanation: Cardiomyocytes are mechanically linked end to end by fascia adherens and desmosomes, and ions pass through gap junctions so the heart contracts as a functional syncytium.

questions.stem: An electron micrograph shows a T tubule between two enlarged sacs of sarcoplasmic reticulum at the boundary between A and I bands. What is this arrangement and in which tissue is it found?

options.text: A diad at the Z disc, in cardiac muscle
An intercalated disc, in cardiac muscle

distractorRationale.b: A diad has one SR cisterna and lies at the Z disc.

questions.explanation: A T tubule flanked by two terminal cisternae forms a triad, located at the A-I junction of skeletal muscle. In cardiac muscle the diad sits at the Z disc.

questions.stem: Compare skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle in terms of cell shape, nuclei, striations and innervation.
markingGuide: Skeletal: long unbranched multinucleate fibres, peripheral nuclei, striated, somatic motor innervation.
Cardiac: branched cells with 1-2 central nuclei, striated, intercalated discs, autonomic modulation.
Smooth: spindle cells with one central nucleus, no striations, autonomic innervation.
Correct pairing of features with each type.
questions.explanation: A full answer pairs each feature with the correct muscle type rather than listing features alone.

questions.stem: Explain why a disorder of gap junction proteins in cardiomyocytes may cause rhythm disturbances, referring to the structure of the intercalated disc.
markingGuide: Intercalated discs link cardiomyocytes end to end.
Fascia adherens and desmosomes give mechanical strength, gap junctions give low-resistance electrical coupling.
Gap junctions let action potentials spread so the myocardium acts as a syncytium.
Defective gap junctions slow or disorganise conduction and can promote arrhythmias.
questions.explanation: Gap junctions are the electrical component of the intercalated disc, so faulty coupling disturbs conduction.

questions.stem: Describe what happens to the A band, I band, H zone and Z-disc spacing when a sarcomere contracts, and explain why using the arrangement of thick and thin filaments.
markingGuide: Thin filaments attach to Z discs and slide over thick filaments.
A band (thick filament length) stays constant.
I band and H zone shorten or disappear.
Z discs move closer so the sarcomere shortens.
M line anchors thick filaments centrally.
questions.explanation: Contraction results from filament sliding, not filament shortening. Only regions defined by absence of overlap change width.
